tools.name: inspect
tools.description: Call this after EVERY edit to a mesh — each bpy script, boolean, join, export — before deciding what to do next. In one sub-second call it answers what is easy to get wrong blind: is it one connected shell or several floating pieces; is it a closed solid (watertight) or are there holes / overlapping faces; how big it is in real metres; which way is up; where the origin sits (base centre, centre, or floating off the object); whether node transforms are applied or mirrored. Read `summary` first. Every finding names a versioned rule (e.g. topo/open-edges from core-geometry@1), says whether it was measured, and carries a likely cause with its confidence plus a concrete fix; the same findings appear in errors[] with alias codes. `front` is always unknown (no honest heuristic exists) unless you declare it. Pass `expect` with what you meant to make ("chair, Z-up, meters, single-shell, 0.4-1.2m tall, front -Y, watertight, origin base") and it is checked as a contract: shell count, watertight, size range, origin are measured and fail as errors; a bare category gives a plausibility warning from a size table with a confidence. profile decides severities: authoring (default: topology problems are warnings, because they are most likely the last edit's doing) or a web budget such as mobile-hero (topology is informational). For per-mesh detail behind a finding use inspect_geometry; for materials, animation and budgets use inspect_all.

path.description: Absolute path to a .glb, .gltf, .usdz, .usda, .usdc or .usd file

category.description: e.g. "chair" — looked up in a coarse size table for a plausibility check (heuristic)

up.description: Authoring up axis. glTF files are Y-up by definition, so Z-up is reported as informational there

units.description: Unit of the numbers in this expectation (the file must be metres)

shells.description: Exact connected-shell count or a range (welded space)

size.description: Range in metres along height (up axis), width (largest across), or largest

expect.description: What you meant to make, free text ("chair, Z-up, single-shell, 0.4-1.2m tall, front -Y") or structured. Adds the intent@1 pack; unparsed tokens are reported

profile.description: Rule profile: authoring or a budget profile mobile-hero | desktop-hero | product-configurator (pin with @N)

topology.description: Welded-space topology pass (shells, watertight, non-manifold). ~70 ms per 150k triangles; when false the topology rules are listed in `skipped`

packs.description: Rule packs to run instead of the profile's: core-geometry | core-scene | intent (pin with @N)

lineage.description: Optional id naming the asset across renames, for the local opt-in usage counter (never sent anywhere)

tools.name: diff
tools.description: What changed between two versions of an asset — including what the edit BROKE by accident. Call it after an edit, with the file you started from and the file you produced, before deciding whether to keep the change. Reports per-part size deltas ("'legs' is 30% narrower along X"), triangle and shell deltas, topology regressions (was watertight, now has 3 open loops), origin drift relative to the geometry, node transform changes, meshes added or removed, and with visual=true a front / side / top / iso render delta (SSIM per view, cameras fixed to the before framing so a size change reads as a change). Read `summary` first; it is written as a change note with regressions first. Findings are diff@1 rules (regressions at warning, neutral changes at info) with causes and fixes, mirrored into errors[]. For a single file, call inspect.

before.description: Absolute path to the earlier version

after.description: Absolute path to the later version

profile.description: Rule profile for severities: authoring or a budget profile

topology.description: Welded topology pass on both files (shells, watertight, open loops, non-manifold deltas)

visual.description: Render four canonical views of both and score SSIM per view (~150 ms per file at 128 px)

lineage.description: Optional id naming the asset across renames, for the local opt-in usage counter (never sent anywhere)

tools.name: validate
tools.description: Does the asset open, and is it well-formed for its target? Returns format, USDZ packaging compliance (stored entries, 64-byte alignment, allowed file types), layer metadata (default_prim, up_axis, meters_per_unit, layer_stack), schema errors, and AR Quick Look compatibility with arkit_issues — every issue with a stable code and prim_path. mode=quick (default) runs no renders and finishes well under a second; mode=full adds analyze_performance and a front render. Call it first on any file, and after every mutation.

path.description: Absolute path to a .glb, .gltf, .usdz, .usda, .usdc or .usd file

profile.description: mode=full only: performance profile for the budget check (default ios_ar)

tools.name: inspect_geometry
tools.description: Per-mesh drill-down behind an `inspect` finding (for the edit loop itself call `inspect`: faster, semantic, named rules). Keyed by prim_path: vertex/face/triangle counts, is_manifold, degenerate faces, normals authored|missing and inverted-normal count, UV sets with out-of-range flags, world bounding box in metres; scene-level bounds, pivot position (pivot_at_base for AR placement) and scale warnings (largest dimension < small_scale or > large_scale). Use it to decide whether an asset needs normals, rescaling or re-pivoting before export.

path.description: Absolute path to a .glb, .gltf, .usdz, .usda, .usdc or .usd file

topology.description: Run the manifold / degenerate edge pass (O(n); skip for speed on huge meshes)

tools.name: inspect_animation
tools.description: Does anything actually move? Clips with time range / fps / duration, animated prims and which properties animate, skeletons (joint_count, bound_meshes, max_influences_per_vertex, unbound_vertex_count), blend shapes with is_driven, root motion. Codes: SKELETON_UNBOUND, MESH_NOT_DEFORMING, BLENDSHAPE_UNDRIVEN, ANIMATION_ZERO_LENGTH, ANIMATION_NO_MOTION. Call it before render_animation_strip or export_usdz on any rigged asset.

path.description: Absolute path to a .glb, .gltf, .usdz, .usda, .usdc or .usd file

tools.name: inspect_materials
tools.description: Materials with shader_type and bound_meshes, unbound_meshes, every texture (resolved, resolution, format, size_bytes, channel, color_space, used_by material+input, memory estimate), missing_textures, texture_memory_estimate_mb, non_power_of_two and oversized (threshold configurable). Codes: TEXTURE_UNRESOLVED, MATERIAL_UNBOUND, MESH_NO_MATERIAL, TEXTURE_OVERSIZED, TEXTURE_NPOT, TEXTURE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED.

path.description: Absolute path to a .glb, .gltf, .usdz, .usda, .usdc or .usd file

oversized_threshold.description: Pixels; TEXTURE_OVERSIZED above this on either axis

tools.name: analyze_performance
tools.description: Totals and estimates (triangles, vertices, draw calls, file size, GPU memory, prim count, scene depth, animation seconds), instancing_candidates, and a budget_check against a profile (ios_ar | visionos | web, a budget profile like mobile-hero, or custom_limits) — each overage names the metric, value, limit and worst_offender_prim_path. Use it to pick targetTriangles for optimize_glb.

path.description: Absolute path to a .glb, .gltf, .usdz, .usda, .usdc or .usd file

profile.description: Performance profile: ios_ar | visionos | web (documented in docs/performance-profiles.md), or a budget profile mobile-hero | desktop-hero | product-configurator[@N]

custom_limits.description: Custom limits (override / replace the named profile): max_triangles, max_vertices, max_draw_calls, max_materials, max_textures, max_file_bytes, max_gpu_memory_mb, max_texture_size, max_texture_bytes, max_prim_count, max_scene_depth

tools.name: render
tools.description: Deterministic software render (no GPU) of any GLB / USDZ / USD: view=front (one straight-on view), thumbnail (one 3/4 view), turntable (N angles tiled into one contact sheet, default 8), or custom (explicit camera position/target/fov). Pass time (seconds) or frame (index at fps) to pose an animated asset. Returns the PNG plus the camera(s) used so you know what you are looking at. Optionally saves the PNG.

path.description: Absolute path to a .glb, .gltf, .usdz, .usda, .usdc or .usd file

camera.description: custom: eye position (world metres), look-at target (default scene centre), vertical fov in degrees (default 40)

frame.description: Animation frame index at fps (alternative to time)

fps.description: Frame rate used to convert frame → time (USD files use their own timeCodesPerSecond)

animation.description: Clip index when the asset has several

out.description: Absolute path to also save the PNG

tools.name: render_animation_strip
tools.description: Contact sheet of an animated asset at the requested frames (stills, labelled with frame and time) so you can verify that it moves the way it should. frames are indices at fps (or pass times in seconds). include_clip=true also writes an animated GIF next to the sheet for human reviewers. Run inspect_animation first to learn the clip range.

path.description: Absolute path to a .glb, .gltf, .usdz, .usda, .usdc or .usd file

frames.description: Frame indices at fps, e.g. [0, 10, 20, 30]. Default: 8 evenly spaced frames over the clip

fps.description: Frame rate for frame → time (USD files use their own timeCodesPerSecond)

include_clip.description: Also write an animated GIF (<out or path>.strip.gif)

out.description: Absolute path to save the contact sheet PNG

tools.name: inspect_all
tools.description: Everything at once for an UNFAMILIAR asset you did not author: validate + inspect_geometry + inspect_animation + inspect_materials + analyze_performance merged into one response, errors deduplicated. Call it once when a file arrives (a download, a generation result). While editing a mesh, call `inspect` instead after each change — it is the fast, rule-based read.

path.description: Absolute path to a .glb, .gltf, .usdz, .usda, .usdc or .usd file

profile.description: Performance profile: ios_ar | visionos | web (documented in docs/performance-profiles.md), or a budget profile mobile-hero | desktop-hero | product-configurator[@N]

custom_limits.description: Custom limits (override / replace the named profile): max_triangles, max_vertices, max_draw_calls, max_materials, max_textures, max_file_bytes, max_gpu_memory_mb, max_texture_size, max_texture_bytes, max_prim_count, max_scene_depth

tools.name: capabilities
tools.description: What this GLBForge install can do right now: versions, which generation providers have keys (FAL_KEY → generate_image_to_3d; MESHY_API_KEY → meshy_*), whether a KTX2 encoder is installed (textureFormat=ktx2), profiles, and the working directory .env is read from. Call it before planning a generation or KTX2 route so you never hit a missing-key error mid-plan.

tools.name: compare_glb
tools.description: Measure how faithfully a candidate GLB matches a reference: visual SSIM over four fixed cameras (gated on the profile floor) plus geometric alignment (point-to-surface chamfer, F-scores, proportion IoU). Returns a reference | candidate | change-heatmap sheet for the weakest view. Use it to judge any optimization, a regenerated asset against the original, or two generators against each other.

reference.description: Absolute path to the reference .glb (e.g. the original)

candidate.description: Absolute path to the candidate .glb (e.g. the optimized file)

profile.description: Budget profile: mobile-hero | desktop-hero | product-configurator; pin a version with name@N (e.g. mobile-hero@1)

textures.description: Include base-color textures in the renders

geometry.description: Also run the geometric alignment score (chamfer, F-scores, IoU). Costs seconds on 100k-tri meshes and up to a minute on multi-million-tri inputs; the visual score alone takes ~5s

tools.name: list_profiles
tools.description: List the web performance budget profiles: triangle/draw-call/texture/file-size/GPU-memory caps, the minimum visual-fidelity SSIM an optimization must keep, the profile version to pin in CI, and (with rationale=true) why each cap is what it is. (AR targets — ios_ar, visionos — live in analyze_performance.)

tools.name: analyze_glb
tools.description: Analyze a GLB/glTF against a web performance budget. Returns a compact report card (score, pass/fail, key numbers, every error + top findings, nextActions) plus a rendered thumbnail; errors[] carries every finding with a code and prim_path. Call inspect_report for full findings/textures/topology, inspect_all for the format-agnostic view. Run before and after any optimization.

profile.description: Budget profile: mobile-hero | desktop-hero | product-configurator; pin a version with name@N (e.g. mobile-hero@1)

preview.description: Rendered PNG of the asset returned with the result: thumbnail (one 3/4 view) | turntable (4 angles tiled 2x2) | none

render.description: Checkpoint render: true = attach a thumbnail even if preview=none, false = no image (overrides preview)

tools.name: inspect_report
tools.description: Drill into an analysis: full findings (with fix suggestions and rule data), per-texture stats, materials, welded-space topology, geometry per primitive, scene/generator facts, or the whole report. Re-analyzes deterministically, so it works on any file at any time.

profile.description: Budget profile: mobile-hero | desktop-hero | product-configurator; pin a version with name@N (e.g. mobile-hero@1)

ruleId.description: findings only: exact rule id or prefix, e.g. "tex" or "perf/file-size"

tools.name: render_preview
tools.description: Render a GLB with the deterministic software rasterizer (no GPU): one thumbnail or a 2x2 turntable of four angles. Use it to look at an asset before deciding, or to verify a result. Optionally saves the PNG. (For front / N-angle / custom cameras, animation frames, and USD inputs use `render`.)

out.description: Absolute path to also save the PNG

tools.name: ship_asset
tools.description: One call from anything to web-ready. A .glb is optimized to the budget and gated. An image is routed: flat artwork forges instantly (free); photographic input returns a routing instruction to call generate_image_to_3d (then optimize_glb the result). Returns the compact report, a geometric fidelity bound, the measured visual-fidelity SSIM (fixed-camera renders before vs after), a sha256 of the output, diff + post_validation, and a thumbnail — or a reference | result | change sheet when SSIM fails. dry_run=true returns the diff without writing.

profile.description: Budget profile: mobile-hero | desktop-hero | product-configurator; pin a version with name@N (e.g. mobile-hero@1)

verify.description: Perceptual (SSIM) verification; a failing SSIM fails the report

preview.description: Rendered PNG of the shipped asset returned with the result: thumbnail (one 3/4 view) | turntable (4 angles tiled 2x2) | none

render.description: Checkpoint render: true = attach a thumbnail even if preview=none, false = no image (overrides preview)

dry_run.description: Compute everything in memory and return the diff it would apply; write nothing

tools.name: audit_directory
tools.description: Analyze every GLB in a directory against a budget profile in one call. Returns a per-file score table plus the failing list — then call optimize_glb on each failure (or ask before bulk-optimizing).

profile.description: Budget profile: mobile-hero | desktop-hero | product-configurator; pin a version with name@N (e.g. mobile-hero@1)

tools.name: optimize_glb
tools.description: Optimize a GLB for web delivery: weld, simplify to the profile triangle budget (bone-aware for skinned/morphing meshes), fill smooth normals, resize/re-encode textures to WebP, meshopt-compress. Writes the optimized file and returns a before/after diff (prims added/removed, properties changed), the measured visual-fidelity SSIM, the compact report, post_validation of the output, a sha256, and a thumbnail — or a reference | result | change sheet when SSIM fails. Every change the pipeline makes on its own (joined prims, generated normals, re-encoded textures) is listed in errors[] with a code. dry_run=true computes everything and writes nothing. Typically 90%+ smaller.

profile.description: Budget profile: mobile-hero | desktop-hero | product-configurator; pin a version with name@N (e.g. mobile-hero@1)

textureFormat.description: webp = smallest file; ktx2 = GPU-resident compression, ~8x less video memory (needs basisu/toktx installed)

verify.description: Perceptual verification: SSIM of fixed-camera renders before vs after, gated on the profile floor; a failing SSIM fails the report

preview.description: thumbnail | turntable | compare (reference | result | change heatmap of the weakest view) | none. A failing SSIM always returns the comparison sheet.

render.description: Checkpoint render: true = attach a thumbnail even if preview=none, false = no image (overrides preview)

dry_run.description: Compute everything in memory and return the diff it would apply; write nothing

tools.name: extrude_image
tools.description: Deterministic 2D graphic -> extruded 3D GLB (no AI, no credits, instant). Traces the image silhouette and projects the source image back on as texture. USE THIS instead of generation for flat artwork: logos, wordmarks, icons, stickers. Use generation for photographic or dimensional subjects. Supports a signage-style bevel on the rims. Returns the mesh stats, diff (the prims created), post_validation, and a thumbnail of the forged piece. dry_run=true writes nothing.

path.description: Absolute path to a PNG/JPEG/WebP with transparent or white background

mode.description: Solid-pixel test: alpha (transparent bg) | luma (white bg). Auto-detected.

bevel.description: Bevel radius in meters (signage look; try depth*0.25)

layers.description: Layered color extrusion: quantize into N color layers at stepped depths (the "layered acrylic" look)

pillow.description: Puffy-sticker dome height in meters (e.g. 0.04); supersedes bevel

emboss.description: Luminance micro-relief in meters — bright artwork rises (try depth*0.15)

preset.description: Material preset for the forged piece

preview.description: Rendered PNG of the forged piece returned with the result: thumbnail (one 3/4 view) | turntable (4 angles tiled 2x2) | none

render.description: Checkpoint render: true = attach a thumbnail even if preview=none, false = no image (overrides preview)

dry_run.description: Compute everything in memory and return the diff it would apply; write nothing

tools.name: export_stl
tools.description: Export a GLB as binary STL for 3D printing — scaled to millimeters, rotated z-up (both reported as AXIS_CONVERTED / SCALE_CONVERTED). Reports watertightness (glbforge-extruded assets are watertight by construction; simplified AI meshes usually are too). Returns a thumbnail of the exported geometry. dry_run=true writes nothing.

preview.description: Rendered PNG of the exported geometry returned with the result: thumbnail (one 3/4 view) | turntable (4 angles tiled 2x2) | none

render.description: Checkpoint render: true = attach a thumbnail even if preview=none, false = no image (overrides preview)

dry_run.description: Compute everything in memory and return the diff it would apply; write nothing

tools.name: export_usdz
tools.description: Export a GLB as USDZ for iOS AR Quick Look: binary usdc layer, UsdPreviewSurface materials, PNG/JPEG textures (WebP is transcoded; KTX2 is rejected), store-only 64-byte-aligned zip. Skinned assets get a UsdSkel skeleton with the first clip sampled at 30 fps; morph targets become UsdSkel blend shapes. Use on the optimized .web.glb. Returns the packed files, diff, post_validation (validate of the written usdz: packaging + AR Quick Look compatibility), every export-time change as a coded entry in errors[], and a thumbnail. dry_run=true writes nothing.

jpeg.description: Encode opaque color textures as JPEG (smaller) instead of PNG

format.description: Layer encoding: binary crate (default, small) or ASCII usda (debugging)

preview.description: Rendered PNG of the exported asset returned with the result: thumbnail (one 3/4 view) | turntable (4 angles tiled 2x2) | none

render.description: Checkpoint render: true = attach a thumbnail even if preview=none, false = no image (overrides preview)

dry_run.description: Compute everything in memory and return the diff it would apply; write nothing

tools.name: generate_image_to_3d
tools.description: True volumetric 3D from a single image via open models on fal.ai GPU inference (needs FAL_KEY — check capabilities first): hunyuan (Hunyuan3D-2, highest quality), trellis (balanced), triposr (fastest). Cheaper than Meshy for most subjects; use Meshy for the richest PBR texturing. Returns a request id — poll generation_status, then download.

image.description: Local path or http(s) URL of the source image

tools.name: generation_status
tools.description: Check an open-model generation (from generate_image_to_3d); when COMPLETED, pass download=true with an out path to save the GLB — the result then includes post_validation and a thumbnail of what was generated. dry_run=true skips writing.

out.description: Absolute output path for the .glb when downloading

preview.description: Rendered PNG of the downloaded model returned with the result: thumbnail (one 3/4 view) | turntable (4 angles tiled 2x2) | none

render.description: Checkpoint render: true = attach a thumbnail even if preview=none, false = no image (overrides preview)

dry_run.description: Compute everything in memory and return the diff it would apply; write nothing

tools.name: meshy_create_task
tools.description: Start a Meshy generation task (needs MESHY_API_KEY — check capabilities first). kind "image-to-3d" takes a local image path or URL; kind "text-to-3d" takes a prompt (geometry preview stage — pass refine_from to texture a finished preview). Returns a task id immediately; poll meshy_task_status (generation takes minutes).

image.description: image-to-3d: local path or http(s) URL

prompt.description: text-to-3d: what to generate; retexture: the style prompt

refine_from.description: text-to-3d: preview task id to refine (texture stage)

input_task_id.description: remesh/retexture: the SUCCEEDED task to operate on

tools.name: meshy_task_status
tools.description: Check a Meshy task: status, progress %, and (when finished) model URLs.

tools.name: meshy_download
tools.description: Download a finished Meshy task's GLB to a local path; returns post_validation and a thumbnail of the model. dry_run=true skips writing.

preview.description: Rendered PNG of the downloaded model returned with the result: thumbnail (one 3/4 view) | turntable (4 angles tiled 2x2) | none

render.description: Checkpoint render: true = attach a thumbnail even if preview=none, false = no image (overrides preview)

dry_run.description: Compute everything in memory and return the diff it would apply; write nothing
